walkthrough: Identify the radiations: $\alpha$-particles are helium nuclei with mass $4u$ and charge $+2e$, while $\gamma$-rays are uncharged electromagnetic photons.

State the rule for ionising power: a larger charge and slower, more strongly interacting particle pulls electrons off more air molecules per mm, so ionisation per unit length is $\alpha > \beta > \gamma$.
State the rule for penetration: energy lost to ionisation is energy lost from the beam, so the most ionizing radiation is stopped quickest and the least ionizing travels furthest.
Apply to air: $\alpha$-particles create about $10^4$ ion pairs per mm and are stopped in a few cm, so they are most ionizing and least penetrating.
Apply to $\gamma$-rays: uncharged photons ionise only via occasional photoelectric or Compton events, so they are least ionizing and can travel many metres in air, so they are most penetrating.
Combine the two correct pairings as most ionizing for $\alpha$-particles and most penetrating for $\gamma$-rays. This is option C
